description: 5.000V precision series reference for the breath sensor supply
notes: +-0.1%, 8ppm/degC AS SPECIFIED (the A suffix is the Standard grade - see the refutation below), ~5ppm/V line reg. The MPXV4006DP is ratiometric so its supply IS its scale factor. Buffered by half of U-BUF | *** 2026-09-21 GRADE REFUTED. THE 'A' SUFFIX IS THE WORSE GRADE. *** SBOS410O (June 2007, revised October 2025) is banked at datasheets/analog/REF5050.pdf. Table 4-2 p.3, verbatim: REF50xxI = grade 'High' = 3ppm/degC, +-0.05%; REF50xxAI = grade 'Standard' = 8ppm/degC, +-0.1%. So REF5050AIDR is +-0.1% and 8ppm/degC, NOT the +-0.05% / 3ppm/degC this row claimed. That is 2x the initial error and 2.7x the drift. EITHER the part becomes REF5050IDR (same package, same pinout, one letter) OR the ratiometric breath scale-factor budget absorbs the difference - and since the whole reason for a separate reference is scale-factor stability, REF5050IDR is almost certainly the right answer. Raised, not decided. NOTE ON PROVENANCE: Table 4-2 is NEW IN REV O, so an older revision may have labelled the grades differently and this row's belief may have had an honest origin; rev M/N was not fetched. FETCH NOTE: ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/ref5050.pdf is a REAL 404 - TI renamed the folder REF50XX -> REF50/REF50E at rev O and broke the symlink. The working URL is ti.com/lit/ds/sbos410/sbos410.pdf

description: Dual RRIO op-amp: breath buffer + reference buffer
notes: SOIC-8. Runs on +12V not 5V - a +12V fault on the BREATH conductor is at the rail so no clamp current, which kills the >=3.3k protection resistor requirement. SAME part as the module op-amps. STABILITY: the reference half drives the sensor's 100nF decoupler ALONE - C-REF-OUT is on the REF5050, not on this output, see figures.yaml cref-out-node. As a bare follower that is still 1.5 degrees of phase margin (100 nF against the specified 375 ohm Zo), so IT IS COMPENSATED, with TI's own dual-feedback network from SBOS737C Figure 56 - R-ISO-REF 37.4R, R-FB-REF 10k taken at VS, R-FBX-REF 100R + C-FB-REF 1nF at this pin. 85.9 degrees. THE OLD IN-LOOP-VS-OUT-OF-LOOP TRADE IS DISSOLVED, not decided: dual feedback gives stability AND exactly zero DC error across R-ISO-REF, so the 2% ratiometric objection to an out-of-loop resistor never has to be paid. See figures.yaml riso-ref-topology | 2026-09-21: SBOS737C is banked at datasheets/analog/OPA2197.pdf, 56pp. TWO CORRECTIONS THAT MATTER. (1) *** OPEN-LOOP OUTPUT IMPEDANCE IS SPECIFIED AND IT IS 375 OHM, NOT THE 75.8 OHM THIS CORPUS BACK-SOLVED. *** EC table p.8 and p.10: 'ZO Open-loop output impedance | f = 1 MHz, IO = 0 A, See Figure 26 | 375 | ohm'. Figure 26 reads ~3.26k at 0.1Hz, 482 at 10Hz, a 375 plateau from 100Hz to 300kHz, 301 at 1MHz and ~73 at 10MHz - so 75.8 ohm is roughly the 10MHz value, i.e. a defensible HF number, but it is NOT TI's specified figure and every pole derived from it moves by ~5x in the wrong direction. (2) *** THE '1 nF MAX CAPACITIVE LOAD' IS AN OPA2197 FIGURE AFTER ALL. *** It is on this part's own p.1 Features ('High Capacitive Load Drive Capability: 1 nF'), in its p.1 Description, and in section 7.3.5 p.22: 'in a unity-gain configuration, directly drives up to 1 nF of pure capacitive load'. The INA828 carries the same headline number by coincidence. The dispute filed against this figure should be closed - and per CLAUDE.md, a correct figure filed as disputed is the dangerous kind, because it stops getting re-checked. Figure 27/28 show 1 nF is a stable-but-ringing limit (~40% overshoot at unity gain), not a 30% threshold; TI recommends a 10-20 ohm isolation resistor and tabulates R_ISO for 45deg/60deg phase margin in Table 3 p.23. CONFIRMED: GBW 10MHz, SR 20V/us, Isc +-65mA, IQ 1mA/amp, ~11.9V swing on +-12V, SOIC-8 DUAL R-thJA 107.9 degC/W (the single OPA197 is 115.8 - different table). NOT-IN-DOCUMENT: the '114 dB PSRR' this corpus cites; TI specifies +-1 uV/V typ and +-3 uV/V max, i.e. 120 dB typ and 110.5 dB worst case. Conclusions unaffected, provenance was not

description: Output and input capacitors on the REF5050
notes: REF5050 VIN bypass and REF5050 VOUT load capacitor - one each, with a 100nF from C-DECOUPLE-CARRIER alongside each. NEITHER IS ON THE BUFFER'S OUTPUT. This is the rail that IS the breath scale factor | 2026-09-21, from the banked SBOS410O. *** THE NODE IS SETTLED: see figures.yaml cref-out-node. *** The part is forced onto the REF5050's own VOUT because the part cannot be built without it - section 8.4.1 p.26 verbatim: 'Confirm that a output capacitor (CL) is connected from VOUT to GND. For output stability, verify that the ESR value of CL less than or equal to 1.5 ohm.' Figure 8-6: CL = 1uF to 50uF for REF50xxI, REF50xxAI. So one of the two is not a choice, and the other is the section 8.4.1 supply bypass (1-10uF) - which accounts for both and leaves nothing for the buffer output. Independently, 10uF there would be 10000x the OPA2197's specified 1 nF capacitive-load limit (SBOS737C p.1 and section 7.3.5 p.22). CONSEQUENCE WORTH WRITING DOWN: the REF5050 now drives only the OPA2197's input bias current (+-20 pA max at 25 C), so its load regulation - 20 ppm/mA typ, 30 max, 50 over temperature, p.7 - contributes ZERO to the breath scale factor, where the other topology would have cost 300 ppm = 1.0 LSB | THE 'MISSING SERIES 1-1.5 OHM RESISTOR' CLAIMED HERE EARLIER IS WITHDRAWN. That read an upper bound as a requirement: section 8.4.1's 'ESR less than or equal to 1.5 ohm' is the STABILITY ceiling, which an X7R satisfies trivially; the 1-1.5 ohm window is a separate NOISE recommendation, and section 9.4.1.1 p.29 says plainly 'A resistor in series with the output capacitor is optional.' Arithmetic: the REF5050's own 10 Hz-1 kHz noise is 0.9 uVrms/V = 4.5 uVrms on 5.000 V, against one ADC LSB at VS of 1.46 mV - a margin of 325x. Gain-peaking on a term 325x below an LSB is not a defect. FIT A 0R/1R0 FOOTPRINT in series with the VOUT capacitor and decide it at E13 with a scope; it is electrically free either way, being in series with a capacitor to ground rather than in the signal path. The TRIM/NR 1uF is DECLINED for the same reason: section 8.3.6 p.26 halves 4.5 uVrms to 2.25 uVrms and lengthens start-up, on a term already 325x below an LSB

description: Isolation resistor, reference buffer dual-feedback network (SBOS737C Fig. 56)
notes: OPA2197 output to SKT-BREATH VS. One of four parts in TI's dual-feedback reference-buffer network; the other three are R-FB-REF, R-FBX-REF and C-FB-REF. INSTRUMENT-SIDE AND UNRETROFITTABLE | 2026-09-21: 10R -> 37.4R, and the justification is replaced rather than amended. SBOS737C section 8.2.3 p.30 Figure 56 'Precision Reference Buffer' is the worked answer for this exact circuit. IT TRANSFERS TO OUR 100 nF DESPITE TI'S 10uF BECAUSE R_ISO IS SET BY Zo, NOT BY C_L - the attenuation R_ISO/(Zo+R_ISO) and the pole-zero ratio both depend only on R_ISO/Zo, and C_L moves both corners together and cancels. 37.4R is Zo/10 against the specified Zo = 375 ohm (p.8). Simulated 85.9 degrees at 896 kHz, and the same model run on Figure 56 as printed returns 87.4 against TI's published 89. DC ERROR ACROSS THIS RESISTOR IS EXACTLY ZERO BY TOPOLOGY - C-FB-REF blocks at DC so no current flows in R-FBX-REF, input current is pA so none flows in R-FB-REF, and the amplifier therefore forces V(VS) = 5.000 V. Its value and tolerance stop mattering; 1% is bought for stock reasons. Power is (10mA)^2 x 37.4 = 3.74 mW in an 0805. THE OLD ROW'S IN-LOOP CHOICE IS REFUTED, NOT SUPERSEDED: in-loop R_ISO buys nothing at ANY value - 1.5 degrees at 10R and 1.5 degrees at 37.4R, the same as fitting nothing. See figures.yaml riso-ref-topology

description: DC feedback resistor, reference buffer - taken at the sensor's VS pin
notes: Part of the reference buffer's dual-feedback network - see R-ISO-REF and figures.yaml riso-ref-topology. INSTRUMENT-SIDE AND UNRETROFITTABLE: the carrier board is inside the sealed body and this network cannot be added later | 10k AND NOT TI'S 1M, deliberately. Two reasons TI's circuit does not have. (1) The guaranteed-over-temperature I_B of 5 nA through 1M is 5 mV = 1000 ppm = 3.4 LSB on a rail that IS the ratiometric scale factor; through 10k it is 50 uV = 0.034 LSB. (2) R_F x C_F sets the HANDOVER frequency above which the loop closes on the amplifier's own output instead of on VS. TI's load is a pure capacitor; ours draws 10 mA, so above the handover any load-current change appears at VS across R-ISO-REF. TI's 1M x 39nF puts it at 4.08 Hz, inside the breath channel. 10k x 1nF puts it at 15.9 kHz, well above the 500 Hz channel, and |Z_out| at VS is then 1.20 ohm at 500 Hz. The R-FB-REF:R-FBX-REF RATIO OF 100:1 IS WHAT MUST BE PRESERVED from TI, not the absolute values

description: AC feedback resistor, reference buffer - taken at the OPA2197 output pin
notes: Part of the reference buffer's dual-feedback network - see R-ISO-REF and figures.yaml riso-ref-topology. INSTRUMENT-SIDE AND UNRETROFITTABLE: the carrier board is inside the sealed body and this network cannot be added later | Scales with R-FB-REF to hold TI's 100:1 ratio, so that above the handover the loop closes on the amplifier output with only 1% of VS leaking in. R_Fx x C_F is 100 ns here against the 3.74 us TI's own rule (R_Fx C_F = R_ISO C_L) would give, and the simulation says it costs nothing - the binding condition is |R_Fx + 1/(2.pi.f C_F)| much less than R_F AT CROSSOVER, which at 896 kHz is 100 + 178 = 205 ohm against 10k, a 49x margin

Part of the reference buffer's dual-feedback network - see R-ISO-REF and figures.yaml riso-ref-topology. INSTRUMENT-SIDE AND UNRETROFITTABLE: the carrier board is inside the sealed body and this network cannot be added later | C0G, because this capacitor sets the handover frequency and an X7R's DC-bias and temperature derating would move it. 1nF at R-FB-REF's 10k gives a 15.9 kHz handover. IT IS ALSO WHY THE DC ERROR IS ZERO: blocking at DC is what leaves R-FB-REF as the only feedback path, so the amplifier servos the SENSOR pin rather than its own output. NOTE FOR THE SPICE DECK: this network leaves the summing node with no DC path except through R-FB-REF, so a simulator needs a leak resistor there for convergence and a real board does not - the amplifier's input leakage provides it
